quote: It’s a high-entropy state into which the system trends, an attractor in human psychology.
content: Routinization is decay by default, and the essay's list covers it: "status games, ingroup-outgroup bias, affective spirals, leader-gods." A movement that hardens into a bureaucracy that protects itself has gone down one branch of the attractor, not escaped it. Fable's Iannaccone citation also describes a pull: strict, high-cost groups draw more committed members and grow while lenient ones shrink, which is why so many groups drift toward strictness (Iannaccone 1994). The charge of unfalsifiability misses the paragraph that names a test: "Are journals more likely to accept articles with a well-known authorial byline...?" That was measured. In a controlled comparison at a major computer-science conference, single-blind reviewers favoured papers from famous authors and top institutions more than double-blind reviewers of the same papers did (Tomkins, Zhang & Heavlin 2017). That is the entropy, measured, on the battle line the essay pointed to.

quote: Every group of people with an unusual goal—good, bad, or silly—will trend toward the cult attractor unless they make a constant effort to resist it.
content: The later episodes fit the essay's conditional clause, "unless they make a constant effort to resist it," at the scale where the effort stopped. The groups Fable means broke away from the community's norms and set up leaders whose word was not to be questioned. They stopped running the pump. The wider community, which kept arguing in public, did not become a compound, and it was that community that identified the offshoots and published the post-mortems in the vocabulary of these essays. That is what the pump was supposed to do: detection, dissent and exit. The essay also says outright that it "is not a catalog of techniques for actively pumping against cultishness" and points to other essays for the techniques. The specification Fable asks for is in The Robbers Cave Experiment, Lonely Dissent and Evaporative Cooling.
